symptom: The browser access host is unavailable
failure_stage: Browser-access authorization setup, before extension transport
observations: All three variables absent in inspected T3-launched Codex process and its CUA MCP process.
All three variables nonempty in inspected desktop-app-launched Codex process; values were not printed or copied.
Bundled require-browser-access.mjs initializes missing executor ID to an empty string.
Browser service then requires a host pipe and verification identity and throws the observed error when either is missing.
The host response must be authenticated and scoped to the current executor, session and turn.
Inspected installed T3 app bundle contains none of these environment names or browser/access protocol strings. This alone does not prove all T3 versions lack support.
changes_made: No browser authorization, plugin, native-host or app configuration changed.
previous_conclusion_corrected: The unified computer-use wrapper lacks its browser authorization host here. This does not prevent the separate installed Chrome plugin from using the extension through its trusted node_repl service.

resolution.bootstrap: var { setupBrowserRuntime } = await import(bootstrap_module); var agent = await setupBrowserRuntime(); await agent.browsers.list();
resolution.verification: Browser type extension, family chrome; opened Netrunner lobby at isolated port 5176, clicked View decks and read updated DOM.
resolution.configuration_changes: None; no authorization settings or code were disabled or altered.
